country.value: uncertain; crest refined in the Netherlands

summary.value: The Polish is an old European crested breed. Nobody knows for sure where it began, but Dutch breeders shaped the big feathered crest that sits on a bony dome on top of the skull. Hens wear a neat round pom-pom, while roosters carry a looser, shaggier mop. Some strains are bearded and some are frizzled. Roosters weigh about 6 pounds and hens about 4.5. Hens lay roughly 150 to 200 white eggs a year, start a little late, and almost never go broody. The birds are calm and friendly but spook easily, because the crest blocks much of their view, so hawks are a real risk. Speaking softly when walking up helps. They handle heat well when given shade but do poorly in cold, wet weather, when the crest can soak or freeze. They suit families who want a showy, gentle bird in a dry, covered run.
